Rule: cfe puts the RIGHT operand of the commutative mul first whenever it holds an array-element or *p load (arr[idx], arr[2], *parr, karr[idx].b, (arr+idx)[0], *(arr+idx)), even when the left one also does (arr2[idx]*3.0 * arr[idx] swaps); member loads (p->a->f, kk.b, (karr+idx)->b) and scalars keep source order. No A spelling can win (scale[0], sub4[0], gCur[0], (*p).f, -(-S), S*1.0, S+0.0, (f64)(f32)S all lose). Context is irrelevant (f32/f64 local, global store, arg). Side effects inside either mul operand ((s = S), (a = arr[idx]), (b = 3.0)) or around the dividend ((sp = S*P)/0.15, sp = E) do not keep the order; only the divisor's does. Real-file probe probe/D5E10.c: ((ProbeF32 *)gKongHoldPutDownAngles + gCurrentCharacterIndex)->v gives fdiff 0, a punned struct view, so not applied. Natural C has no f32-array read that cfe treats as light: site stays FAKE.
